claims.assertion: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:03:00 while GPS placed him 39 m from the pickup point, so the arrival condition in NS-1(i)-(ii) is satisfied on the record (F6).

After that tap the driver remained within 200 m of the pickup point for 6 min 10 s until cancellation, exceeding the 3-minute NS-1(iii) threshold, and the GPS track shows him stationary from 09:03:00 to 09:09:10 at 39 m from the pickup, so there is no sampling gap that would force a manual referral (F3, F6).

The platform-side timeline independently records arrival at 09:02:40 and cancellation 6 min 30 s later (F5), and the rider cancelled 9 min 0 s after acceptance, so the $6.61 fee on record meets the NS-0/NS-4 branch for a rider cancellation beyond the 3-minute grace period (F4, F7).

This is an immediate booking (RydeX, matched and cancelled the same morning), so the rider's cancellation falls under NS-4 rather than the scheduled-ride branch; the fee stands unless a NS-7 waiver is granted (F4, F7).

The rider's only excuse on the record is being held up upstairs after saying "give me 2 more minutes", which the driver already exceeded; Ryde publishes no free-cancellation right for rider delay and NS-8 is informational only, so no live clause excuses the fee (F10, F11, F13).

No condition of NS-2 is met: arrival was recorded (F6), it was within 200 m (F6), and the wait after the tap exceeded 3 minutes (F3), so a full refund is not owed and no account flag attaches to the driver for this cancellation.

The dispute was filed after the 09:09:10 cancellation of the same trip and within the 30-day window, which is the only procedural route open to the rider; any amount granted would be issued as a Ryde voucher rather than cash (F4, F7).
The charge itself is correctly computed: $6.61 with no surge multiplier, i.e. the published cancellation fee only, with no unpublished add-on for the rider to contest (F7, F8).
The rider's 90-day record shows 3 disputes and 0 upheld, so there is no pattern of past merit to support an account action on the rider side; the driver likewise has 0 upheld disputes (F17, F18).
The exchange contains no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation by either side, so the case does not require escalation under SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 (F9, F10, F11, F13).

weaknesses: The decisive system records cut both ways and are the strongest evidence against us: F6 shows the driver tapped "I'm Here" 39 m from the pickup and F3 shows he then stayed there 6 min 10 s, satisfying NS-1(i)-(iii) by a wide margin, while F5 gives an independent platform arrival at 09:02:40.

The rider's own honesty in the complaint and in the chat (F10 "give me 2 more minutes", F11 the driver saying he waited 5 minutes and called twice, F13 the driver's statement of over 6 minutes' wait and two unanswered calls) confirms the rider did not come down before cancelling, which is exactly the conduct NS-1/NS-4 charge for; no clause gives a free cancellation for rider-side delay (NS-8 is informational only).

There is no driver-side defect to pivot to: F16 shows fair weather, F15 shows no traffic incidents, and F7/F8 show a clean $6.61 at 1.0x surge with no unpublished add-on, so FARE-1 offers no partial-refund route either.
The rider's profile at F17 (3 disputes in 90 days, 0 upheld) gives the judge no track record of meritorious complaints and cannot itself support any finding.
